claim_text: Despite this, we made significant progress in decarbonisation through the commissioning of the North Star Junction solar farm which generated 180 GWh, meeting 25 per cent of Iron Bridge’s current electricity needs, and helped avoid additional emissions from the Solomon gas power station.

Overall PEC emissions intensity has improved by 18 per cent in FY25 with the introduction of this 100MW solar farm.；Group Scope 1 and 2 emissions (location-based) FY25 3.02 FY24 2.72 VARIANCE 10.9%.；Group Scope 1 and 2 location-based emissions intensity FY25 0.015 FY24 0.014 VARIANCE 7.1%.；The 10.9 per cent increase in Scope 1 and 2 emissions combined with a 3.5 per cent increase in ore produced, resulted in a seven per cent increase in emissions intensity in FY25.
label: Suspected Greenwash
llm_reason: The claim’s central assertion is that commissioning the North Star Junction solar farm drove “significant progress in decarbonisation” by (1) generating 180 GWh, (2) meeting 25% of Iron Bridge’s current electricity needs, and (3) helping avoid additional emissions from the Solomon gas power station. The evidence directly supports the specific generation and share figures: it states the solar farm “generated 180 GWh” and “meeting 25 per cent of Iron Bridge’s current electricity needs.” However, the evidence does not substantiate the emissions-avoidance outcome (“helped avoid additional emissions from the Solomon gas power station”) with any quantified avoided-emissions amount, baseline, or comparison. Additionally, the broader “significant progress in decarbonisation” framing is not clearly supported by the provided emissions results, which show increases in Total Group Scope 1 emissions (2.64 vs 2.36 MtCO₂-e, +12.0%) and Group Scope 1 and 2 (location-based) emissions (3.02 vs 2.72 MtCO₂-e, +10.9%) and an increase in location-based emissions intensity (0.015 vs 0.014 tCO₂-e/wmt, +7.1%).
